issues.description: Class element: Animal constructor and its name accessor methods. The problem statement (UML and explicit note) requires the Animal constructor and the getName()/setName() accessors to be protected (UML shows protected '#', and the text explicitly states: "implement the name getter and setter with protected visibility"). The solution implementation makes all three members public: constructor 'public Animal(String name)' and methods 'public String getName()', 'public void setName(String newName)'. This mismatch between the exercise specification and the provided solution code can mislead students about the intended visibility and inheritance design and may cause them to implement the wrong access modifiers.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the artifacts consistent. Either (A) change the solution and template to use protected visibility for the Animal constructor and the name accessor methods, i.e. 'protected Animal(String name)', 'protected String getName()', and 'protected void setName(String newName)'; or (B) update the problem statement/UML to accept public visibility and remove the explicit protected note. Prefer option A to match the current specification: update the solution and template Animal.java signatures to use 'protected' and re-run tests/examples to ensure no access problems arise.
